---
title: "Measuring model performance"
---

This project documents how to measure the performance of predictive models,
working through every method on real models fitted to real data. Each page
answers one question about a model, shows the method on our examples, and
explains when it misleads.

## The examples

Most pages use the **French motor insurance dataset** (freMTPL2, about 680,000
policies) with two targets:

| Target | Type | Question |
|---|---|---|
| `HasClaim` | binary (0/1) | Will this policy have a claim? |
| `PurePremium` | continuous, weighted by exposure | What claim cost per year should we expect? |

For each target we compare a **GLM** (the traditional baseline) with a
**gradient boosting machine (GBM)**, plus a **Null** model that predicts the
average for everyone. A few pages also use **California Housing**, a
continuous target with a strong signal, where standard error metrics behave
as textbooks describe. See [Data and models](docs/foundations/data-and-models.qmd).

## How the pages are organized

Metrics are grouped by the question they answer rather than listed by name:

- **Classification at a threshold:** is the yes/no decision right?
  ([confusion matrix](docs/binary/confusion-matrix.qmd))
- **Discrimination:** does the model rank cases correctly?
  ([ROC and AUC](docs/binary/roc-auc.qmd),
  [precision–recall](docs/binary/precision-recall.qmd))
- **Calibration:** do predicted probabilities match observed frequencies?
  ([calibration and scoring rules](docs/binary/calibration.qmd))
- **Error size:** how far off are the predictions?
  ([error metrics](docs/continuous/error-metrics.qmd),
  [deviance](docs/continuous/deviance.qmd))
- Lift charts, model comparison and drift: *coming next*.

## Working with the code

All metric and plotting code lives in the `modelperf` package (`src/modelperf/`)
and is tested against scikit-learn. Pages only call it, so explanations and
implementations stay in sync.

```bash
uv sync                  # install the environment
uv run pytest            # check the metrics
uv run quarto preview    # build and serve the site locally
```

The first page you render downloads the data and fits all models (about a
minute); fitted models are cached in `artifacts/`.
